item.base_system: Homogenized Al0.7CoCrFeNi alloy (Ho alloy) with dual-phase lamellae microstructure
item.processing: 6 GPa pressure, 1473 K temperature, maintained for 2 hours in a hexahedron-anvil-press apparatus
item.structure_change: Transformation from dual-phase lamellae to a hierarchically patterned microstructure with hexagonal-like structural units and coherent FCC/B2 interfaces
item.property_change: Tensile strength increased to ~1150 MPa (nearly 100% enhancement) and tensile ductility increased to 36% compared to the Ho alloy
item.attributed_mechanism: HPHT-induced formation of a hierarchically patterned microstructure with coherent interfaces promotes multiple deformation mechanisms and relieves stress concentration at interfaces
quotes: We report an initially strong-yet-brittle eutectic high entropy alloy simultaneously doubling its strength to 1150 MPa and its tensile ductility to 36% after the HPHT treatment.
Such strength-ductility synergy is attributed to the HPHT-induced formation of a hierarchically patterned microstructure with coherent interfaces, which promotes multiple deformation mechanisms

records.text: Intervention effect. Base system: Homogenized Al0.7CoCrFeNi alloy (Ho alloy) with dual-phase lamellae microstructure. Intervention: High-pressure and high-temperature (HPHT) treatment. Processing: 6 GPa pressure, 1473 K temperature, maintained for 2 hours in a hexahedron-anvil-press apparatus. Test conditions: Room temperature tensile testing. Structure change: Transformation from dual-phase lamellae to a hierarchically patterned microstructure with hexagonal-like structural units and coherent FCC/B2 interfaces. Property change: Tensile strength increased to ~1150 MPa (nearly 100% enhancement) and tensile ductility increased to 36% compared to the Ho alloy. Mechanism: HPHT-induced formation of a hierarchically patterned microstructure with coherent interfaces promotes multiple deformation mechanisms and relieves stress concentration at interfaces. Evidence: measured. Quote: "We report an initially strong-yet-brittle eutectic high entropy alloy simultaneously doubling its strength to 1150 MPa and its tensile ductility to 36% after the HPHT treatment."

item.processing: 6 GPa pressure, 1473 K temperature, 2 hours duration
item.structure_change: Interface changed from a transition layer of ~10 nm thickness to a coherent interface with a mismatch factor of 0.004
item.property_change: Fracture mode changed from catastrophic brittle interfacial fracture to uniform distribution of isolated microcracks
item.attributed_mechanism: Coherent FCC/B2 interface helps relieve stress concentration at the interfaces, thereby arresting interfacial cracking
quotes: More importantly, the HPHT-induced microstructure helps relieve stress concentration at the interfaces, thereby arresting interfacial cracking commonly observed in traditional eutectic high entropy alloys.

item.processing: 6 GPa pressure, 1473 K temperature, 2 hours duration
item.test_conditions: Room temperature tensile testing up to 35% strain
item.structure_change: Preservation of hierarchically patterned microstructure; formation of microbands, high-density dislocation walls (HDDWs), and deformation twins
item.property_change: High uniform tensile elongation (~36%) and high true fracture stress (~1570 MPa); work-hardening capability is more pronounced and stable
item.attributed_mechanism: Multiple deformation mechanisms (dislocations, stacking faults, microbands, deformation twins) activated at multiple length scales due to coherent interfaces
quotes: Notably, the featured hierarchically patterned microstructure is well preserved during loading, which can even be observed faintly on the fracture surface after the extended uniform elongation
More importantly, the HPHT alloy exhibits a high true fracture stress of ~1570 MPa, which is considerably higher than those of Ac, Ac+HPHT and Ho alloys, respectively.
Such progressive activation of multiple plastic deformation mechanisms in both FCC and BCC phases of the HPHT alloy is in distinct contrast to the case of Ho alloy

item.processing: 6 GPa pressure, 1473 K temperature, 2 hours duration
item.structure_change: GND density increased significantly in both FCC and B2 phases; homogeneous distribution of GNDs at 35% strain
item.property_change: Improved capability of dislocation storage; uniform deformation distribution compared to Ho alloy
item.attributed_mechanism: Coherent interface allows dislocation transfer and coordinates deformation between phases, leading to strain delocalization
quotes: Moreover, the GND densities in the HPHT alloy are much higher than those in the Ho alloy, indicating improved capability of dislocation storage in the HPHT-treated alloy.

Upon further loading, the GND density of the B2 phase increases much faster than that of the FCC phase, eventually resulting in an identical value of GND density in both phases at 35% strain, consistent with a homogeneous plastic deformation distribution
Dislocations preferentially initiate in the softer FCC phase, and subsequently are allowed to transfer into the harder B2 phase due to the highly coherent interface

item.processing: 6 GPa pressure, 1473 K temperature, 2 hours duration
item.structure_change: Formation of isolated microcracks cut through B2 phase; twisted fracture paths; unbroken ligaments near fracture surface
item.property_change: Enhanced tensile elongation due to delocalized damage accumulation and arrest of crack propagation
item.attributed_mechanism: High density of microcracks and twisted fracture paths prevent crack coalescing into elongated voids; unbroken ligaments shield crack propagation
quotes: Specifically, numerous isolated microcracks cut through the B2 phase and the fracture paths were twisted among the two phases in the HPHT-treated alloy, preventing crack coalescing into elongated voids.
Besides, a number of unbroken ligaments were observed near the fracture surface, which is believed to shield crack propagation.
The enhanced tensile elongation of the HPHT-treated alloy can thus be related to the delocalized damage accumulation and arrest of crack propagation.

item.processing: 6 GPa pressure, 1473 K temperature, 2 hours duration
item.structure_change: Formation of extended stacking faults (SFs), microbands, and deformation twins (DTs) in both FCC and B2 phases
item.property_change: Superior strength-ductility synergy compared to conventional hot isostatic pressing and thermal-mechanical treatments
item.attributed_mechanism: Coherent interface holds a key to the activation of multiple deformation mechanisms, including SFs, microbands and deformation twins
quotes: Such HPHT-induced synergistic enhancement in strength and ductility is not observed in our experiments with conventional hot isostatic pressing treatment (Supplementary Fig. 5 ) and thermal-mechanical treatment (Supplementary Fig. 6 ).

The hierarchically patterned structure with the coherent interface (Fig. 1 h–l) not only confines dislocation slip, but more importantly, it also provides a route to accommodate plasticity through the activation of multiple deformation mechanisms

item.processing: 6 GPa pressure, 1473 K temperature, 2 hours duration
item.structure_change: Slip transfer between FCC and B2 phases; numerous dislocation-SF interactions; dislocations on both sides of the interface
item.property_change: Less coherent FCC/B2 interface after fracture; uniform deformation of the alloy
item.attributed_mechanism: Uniform deformation is strongly related to the compatible deformation of the B2 phase, associated with high-density dislocations after fracture
quotes: These results indicate that the uniform deformation of the HPHT-treated alloy is strongly related to the compatible deformation of the B2 phase, which is found to be associated with high-density dislocations after fracture
The HPHT-treated alloy with a hierarchically patterned microstructure exhibits distinctive multiple deformation mechanisms, including dislocations, stacking faults, microbands and deformation twins.

item.processing: HPHT treatment in self-designed hexahedron-anvil-press apparatus
item.test_conditions: Not specified in main text (referenced in Supplementary Fig. 22)
item.attributed_mechanism: HPHT strategy can be generally applied to other alloy systems for synergistic improvement
quotes: In view of the adjustable pressure, temperature, and chamber size of the self-designed hexahedron-anvil-press apparatus, the HPHT strategy can be generally applied to pure metal copper (Supplementary Fig. 22 ) and other alloy systems
We further demonstrate that the HPHT treatment can be easily extended to other alloy systems for synergistic improvement of strength and ductility.
These findings suggest a new direction of research in employing HPHT techniques to help develop next generation structural materials.
